first_party_findings: No reviewed API/embedding-worker/audio-worker path directly dispatches native cp/mv/install/sed/tar or the backup/restore/upgrade shell helpers. Docker cp references invoke the Docker engine, and pip/uv install references are not the native install program.

Helper_Scripts/upgrade.sh uses operator repo paths, git state and a timestamp backup destination; git rev-parse runs before cp -a. This is not evidence that ordinary worker jobs perform privileged directory ACL changes.
App entrypoint moves adjacent temporary environment files at startup using server-selected paths; read-only sed formats errors. No request-controlled checkpoint or ACL path is inferred from this.

The two worker recipes do not copy Helper_Scripts and dispatch fixed embedding stages or audio_transcribe jobs. Provider/native consumer closure and effective deployment directory ownership remain unproved.
The app recipe specifies UID 10001; worker recipes lack USER. Neither root process presence nor a callable library proves the advisory prerequisites. No blanket current-use ACL exclusion is added.
limits: No package installation, image build/pull/run, native utility execution, exploit payload or race test.
Source and ELF analysis only. Full backend image filesystem, privileges, ACL-capable third-party consumer closure and attacker control remain unbound.

package_binding.origin: Official Debian binary package matching retained SBOM version; not extracted from backend image

source_findings.debian_patch: gnulib-nfs-acl adds an EOPNOTSUPP/source-ACL check, not a switch to get_permissions.
source_findings.finding: The default USE_XATTR copy branch uses attr_copy_fd with valid descriptors or attr_copy_file for pathname copies. Debian builds with libattr, and exact cp/mv/install import both attr copy APIs but no acl_get_file/acl_get_fd. The ordinary directory xcopy_acl path cannot be attributed to libacl merely because the binary links it.
Regular-file copy opens descriptors and supplies the destination descriptor to ownership, copy-ACL and set-ACL paths.

A separate ownership-preservation operation on a pre-existing non-symlink directory with changed owner/group can invoke set_owner with descriptor -1; when preserve_mode/move_mode/set_mode applies, qset_acl passes a mode-derived permission context to set_permissions and pathname acl_set_file. This prevents a descriptor-only conclusion for every utility operation. It does not establish an attacker-controlled pathname or actual invocation in these deployed workers.
Non-regular preserve-mode/move copying goes through xcopy_acl (the libattr branch); explicit mode and no-preserve-mode paths can separately invoke pathname xset_acl.

approval_basis: Requester authorized supported exclusions in the conversation; rmusser01 owns the record and PR2869 is the review location. No new GitHub approval comment claimed.
